On Fri, Jun 15, 2028 at 08:47 Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com> wrote:
> Ben — can you run the export and include the tokenization breakdown? Please include internal call IDs and the edge hostname for correlation.

Hi all — export attached. The CSV contains per-request rows with: timestamp (ms), request_id, session_id, model, embed_tokens, origin_ip (obfuscated), edge_host, and kernel_tag. A couple of preliminary notes from a first pass:
- There is a concentrated cluster between 22:07 and 22:35 UTC where ~78% of the extra embed units are concentrated. Those rows have sequential request_ids that look like batched replays (request ids with repeated prefix).
- edge_host shows calls routed through edge-bk02-eu which matches shard maintenance logs at 22:06 UTC. I don't see a platform-triggered bulk replay job in our scheduler; however, the edge-maintenance window did cause an unusual retry pattern for clients using non-idempotent retry logic.

Hypothesis: a client integration using a naive retry loop (no idempotency key) retried a batched request set when a transient error occurred during that maintenance window, producing a burst of near-duplicate calls that appear as heavy embedding consumption.

What I need from HoloApps: any client-side job logs that show retry loops or cron-based batch runs in the 22:00-23:00 UTC window. If HoloApps can confirm a misconfigured retry/backoff, we can mark the spike as customer-triggered.

If HoloApps cannot produce evidence but we find server-side duplication, we'll propose a remedial credit and coordinate VAT reversal.

Attachments: usage_export_20280614_overnight.csv (CSV, 2.1 MB)

—
Ben Carter
Billing Operations 
Redwood Inference
From: Caroline Morris <caroline@holoapps.com>

Date: Sun, 17 Jun 2028 16:45:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Unexplained overnight embed spike - holding payment pending reconciliation

Thanks for the quick work and the CSV, Ben. We pulled our job-scheduler logs and confirmed that a nightly batch job (transformer_embed_backfill) retried aggressively after a 502 at 22:05 UTC — the job has a bug that retries the whole batch without deduplication. That aligns exactly with the request_id prefixes in your export.

Given that, we'll: 
- Accept the usage as customer-triggered. We will rework the backfill to use idempotency keys by end of week.
- Proceed to clear the invoice. However, we need a short reconciliation doc from Redwood stating the root cause of the spike and that the spike will not be re-billed retrospectively (we may need to show that to our procurement team).

Kimberly — can Redwood provide a short note we can attach to our PO/finance system confirming the findings (CSV match, times, and that VAT will stay as invoiced since it's customer-triggered)?

Jordan / Ben — if you can send a one-page reconciliatory note (signed by Redwood billing) and the CSV we can attach the artifacts and release payment.

Appreciate the transparency here.

Best,
